question: After every host supplies a canonical execution identity, should a completed low-risk `allow-once` model verdict be reusable for later identical requests during one reviewer instance?
rationale: This intentionally lets a later exec request bypass a fresh model review, so the acceptable lifetime and identity boundary are authorization policy rather than a purely mechanical implementation choice.

options.title: Approve tightly bound reuse
options.body: Permit reuse only after node and gateway execution identities are included, focused host tests pass, and configured runtime proof shows the intended hit and miss behavior.

options.title: Keep per-request review
options.body: Reject verdict reuse and retain one model completion for every ask-requiring exec request to preserve the current authorization cadence.

options.title: Limit reuse to gateway
options.body: Allow memoization only where the gateway already provides a resolved executable identity, leaving node-host requests uncached until equivalent binding exists.

recommendation.title: Approve tightly bound reuse
recommendation.body: Permit reuse only after node and gateway execution identities are included, focused host tests pass, and configured runtime proof shows the intended hit and miss behavior.
